inputs: symmetric pointer and keyboard modal probes

findings.criterion: A06 modal Escape and focus restoration
findings.title: WebKit pointer-opened task dialog does not return focus to its invoker
findings.impact: After opening New task with a pointer and dismissing with Escape, focus stays on BODY instead of New task. Subsequent keyboard navigation restarts from the page rather than the invoking control.
refutationChecks: The dialog actually closes; the remaining failure is focus restoration.
Focus is still BODY after 550 ms, ruling out an asynchronous close-event observation.
Genuine keyboard opening restores focus correctly; the issue is not generalized to all keyboard use.
Chromium passes both pointer and keyboard paths.
The paired app passes all eight identical probes.
Positive and deliberately focus-losing fixtures validate the A06 observer.
sourceEvidence: artifact/app.js:238 stores document.activeElement, which is BODY after WebKit pointer activation.
artifact/app.js:292 chooses that connected BODY as return target instead of the invocation button.

findings.criterion: A08 useful visible error and atomic rejection
findings.refutation: Malformed and unsupported-schema imports preserve the board and display useful errors. The original oracle missed the visible equivalent phrases not valid JSON and Import could not be completed. Corrected positive and silent-error negative controls passed, and the identical A08 rerun passes all four environments for each app.

adjudicatedExecutionSummary.method: Original complete matrix plus a symmetric corrected A08 rerun in all four environments. Original reports and hashes retained.

exploratoryFindings.contractAmbiguity: The brief reserves the select value all for the All projects sentinel while allowing any nonempty project string, including all. This edge was not in the predeclared concrete fixtures; selecting the distinct project option should still be distinguishable from selecting the sentinel.
exploratoryFindings.impact: The valid project named all cannot be isolated; selecting it displays unrelated projects too. Stored records are unchanged.
repro: In an isolated context load the same valid two-task board used for both apps: project all and project Atlas.
Select the actual project option labelled all (selectedIndex 1), not the All projects sentinel.
Compare rendered task IDs and saved bytes.

adjudication.scopeLimit: The primary score covers 16 predefined contract groups. Exploratory edge findings are reported separately and do not alter that score. Neither is a universal security/accessibility/design certification.

adjudication-focus/results.json.criterion: A06 modal close and focus restoration
adjudication-focus/results.json.purpose: Refute action timing and compare pointer vs genuine keyboard opening before deciding whether the observed WebKit failure is a product issue.

exploratory-project-sentinel/selection-t.purpose: Refute incorrect selector or option ambiguity; diagnostic capture only, original fixture and primary scores unchanged.

designReview.method: Single qualitative review of actual captured desktop and mobile pixels. No numerical aesthetic score.

observations.observation: The desktop uses a narrow workspace/project rail, a serif introductory heading, three summary cards, a wide search field and three task columns. Cream surfaces, sage borders, dark green controls and small status/priority accents recur consistently.
observations.implication: The app has a coherent identity and a readable grouping of workspace, summary, controls and tasks. The project list also gives context to the task cards.

observations.observation: Task cards put date, compact status selector and edit/delete controls on a shared bottom row. This keeps multiple cards visible, but project labels, tags, dates, sidebar details and summary captions use small, fine text.
observations.implication: The board uses space efficiently, while secondary information and small action icons demand closer reading than the bold task titles.

observations.observation: The centered form separates task title and project from a two-column status/priority row, followed by due date and tags. Required markers and input guidance are visible, and the title field has a strong focus outline. Cancel and Create task are differentiated.
observations.implication: The layout supports a straightforward entry sequence and makes the focused control clear. Static appearance does not prove complete focus trapping or assistive-technology behavior.

observations.observation: Malformed JSON produces a prominent warm-tinted alert above the main heading, with an explicit failure title, a file-format explanation and a Dismiss button. The existing board remains visible below it.
observations.implication: The error is hard to overlook and gives a recovery direction. The capture receipt confirms unchanged stored bytes for this input; the visible alert could also state that preservation explicitly.

observations.observation: The active search shows one matching task and a Clear filters control, but empty status columns say Room for the next step and Completed work will land here. The summary still shows existing completed tasks outside the filter.
observations.implication: Those empty-state messages sound like an empty board rather than excluded search results. Context-specific wording such as No matching tasks would make the filtering state clearer.

observations.observation: The mobile view keeps a full-width New task button, three summary cards, search and filters within the opening screen; the top of the first status column reaches its lower edge. Primary content fits the width, but metadata, summary captions and filter text are small.
observations.implication: The compact arrangement brings board navigation into view sooner, at the cost of finer text. A complete task card still requires scrolling, and this single capture does not evaluate the remainder of the mobile board.

mobileLayoutObservation.note: The width values come from the capture receipt; they are not an aesthetic score. The first status column begins at the bottom of this viewport.

limits: Only the supplied captured states were reviewed. Mobile coverage here is the initial viewport, not a complete mobile walkthrough.
Static screenshots cannot establish all keyboard behavior, screen-reader output, motion quality, data safety or import correctness. Those need the separate behavioral rubric.
The board counts and progress percentages belong to this fictional seeded application, not benchmark performance or product adoption.
Anchored screenshots preserve actual viewport framing; partial surrounding content does not by itself imply source-page clipping.
No condition mapping was inspected, no candidate code was changed and no numerical aesthetic score or causal improvement claim is assigned.

processReview.summary: The baseline app run expanded an initially passing workflow suite, exposed modal-focus trouble, edited the implementation and retested.

observations.observed: The public plan named local-board implementation, storage recovery, accessible editing and failure-path verification before source creation.
After the first workflow suite passed, the candidate tightened import types/tag preservation and added explicit boundary and failure checks.

The trace records a dialog-protocol failure and a modal-focus assertion failure. A source edit added explicit focus wrapping; subsequent workflow and edge-suite runs exited successfully. The trace does not establish a single cause for the dialog error.
The final record includes syntax checks, browser artifacts and explicit local-storage/Chrome limits.

limits: An initially passing main suite did not cover all subsequently found edge cases.
Candidate test-harness dialog errors occurred; they must not automatically be attributed to application defects.
The same candidate authored the app, tests and self-report.
This descriptive process audit was requested after outcomes existed. It is retrospective and exploratory, not a preregistered process endpoint.
The methods reviewer knows condition assignments; this review is not blinded. Separate proof/design reviewers have their own blinding procedures.
Only public progress messages, observable tool actions, check exits and retained artifact evidence are summarized. No hidden reasoning is inferred or published.
There is no process score, tool-call leaderboard or causal claim. More messages, calls, checks or elapsed time do not imply a better process.
The baseline retains native Codex instructions and the same common trial directions. It is not an unstructured or instruction-free model.
Delegation, external services and auxiliary model calls were prohibited for both conditions. Full orchestration, provider selection, collaboration and autonomous end-to-end deployment are unmeasured.
Treatment includes three or four pinned contracts plus a repository snapshot. Observed behavior cannot be assigned to an individual Fabius rule from this design.
Candidate-authored tests and self-reported passes are process evidence, not substitutes for the independent acceptance and proof checks.
Coverage includes all 12 finalized valid runs from the planned three-task, two-condition, two-repeat study. The two preserved setup attempts are documented separately.
